WWW-Authenticate: Digest qop="auth", realm="DS-39DED0D1", nonce="MASKED-NONCE-RET1", stale="false", domain="::"

<userCheck><statusValue>401</statusValue><statusString>Unauthorized</statusString><lockStatus>unlock</lockStatus><unlockTime>0</unlockTime><retryLoginTime>6</retryLoginTime></userCheck>

INVENTED-BUT-LABELLED — NOT A DEVICE CAPTURE. (card t_a3521d8a)
Shape (b): the nonce WAS retired, but the answer spells `stale="false"` while still
advertising a fresh nonce. This is the shape a client that trusts the `stale` flag
would get wrong (RFC 7235: stale=false means "do not assume the nonce aged out"), and
it is credible on this firmware precisely because the recorded
`digest_challenge_401.txt` shows Hikvision `webs` spelling stale in lowercase and
always sending the field. Same header/body style as that fixture.
Served by: FakeDevice(retire_shape=RETIRE_STALE_FALSE).
Client outcome (probe, docs/FINDINGS-t_a3521d8a.md F1): survived inside httpx —
`auth_flow` never parses `stale` at all (gotchas §1.5), so it re-pays this challenge
exactly like the stale="true" one. Pinning the two shapes separately keeps the claim
"we do not care how the device spells stale" from being an assumption.
